doc: Before/after queries for docs/plans/field-types.md, against weft's own shard stats (the busiest weft-owned source with per-query timings: q_count, q_mean_ms, q_max_ms, q_rows every ~10s per shard). The range is fixed and in the past so results are stable between runs. 'targets' benefit from field facts once jq locators exist; 'controls' must not change.

queries.why: numeric filter on a top-level key: slow-query windows
numeric filter, selective: windows with query errors
numeric filter on a float: volume fullness
numeric filter feeding head: when were the slow windows
sort -n | tail -n 1: the single worst query window
keyed max per shard: worst query time by shard (key first: field 2 is not provably numeric, so this stays unoptimized)
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.shard_id, .q_max_ms] | @tsv' | awk '{ if ($2 > m[$1]) m[$1] = $2 } END { for (k in m) print k, m[k] }' | sort

queries.why: keyed sum per shard: queries served by shard (key first: field 2 is not provably numeric, so this stays unoptimized)
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.shard_id, .q_count] | @tsv' | awk '{ s[$1] += $2 } END { for (k in s) print k, s[k] }' | sort

queries.why: keyed sum per shard: rows returned by shard (key first: field 2 is not provably numeric, so this stays unoptimized)
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.shard_id, .q_rows] | @tsv' | awk '{ s[$1] += $2 } END { for (k in s) print k, s[k] }' | sort

queries.why: keyed sum with the value first, so field 1 is provably numeric (see field-types.md, shift hazard)
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.q_count, .shard_id] | @tsv' | awk '{ s[$2] += $1 } END { for (k in s) print k, s[k] }' | sort

queries.why: keyed sum with the value first
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.q_rows, .shard_id] | @tsv' | awk '{ s[$2] += $1 } END { for (k in s) print k, s[k] }' | sort

queries.why: keyed max with the value first
queries.pipeline: cat /log/weft/shard/stats.log | jq -r '[.q_max_ms, .shard_id] | @tsv' | awk '{ if ($1 > m[$2]) m[$2] = $1 } END { for (k in m) print k, m[k] }' | sort
